title: A reminder for those of understanding
summary: New Hijri year editorial timed to Muharram, using Hajj and Grand Mosque imagery. Argues the umma must return to the foundations the early generations lived by, framing the prophetic method as a single straight path against which all alternatives are deviation. Builds on the hadith of the straight path (Ibn Mas'ud) and Quran 6:153 to argue there is one path and many misleading ways. Rejects the rival 'methods of change': pacifism, democracy, modernity, nationalism, and the concepts of 'coexistence' and 'the bond of humanity'. Claims disbelievers wage a methodical ideological war through Muslims' own children, more dangerous than military war, aimed at erasing the distinction between Muslim and non-Muslim. Insists Muslim, Christian, Hindu, Buddhist, Zoroastrian, Shia and atheist are not equal. Exhorts a return to the way of Ibrahim through tawhid, loyalty and disavowal, migration and jihad.
keyClaims: There is one straight path (the prophetic method) and all other ways are deviation, each with a devil calling to it.
Disbelievers wage a methodical ideological war through Muslims' own children that is more dangerous than military war.
Concepts of coexistence and the bond of humanity are tools to dissolve the distinction between Muslim and non-Muslim.
Muslim and non-Muslim are not equal, contradicting pluralist and humanist framings.
Salvation lies in returning to the way of Ibrahim through tawhid, loyalty and disavowal, migration and jihad.
significanceAssessment: A doctrinal anchoring editorial rather than an operational one, using the Hijri new year to reassert IS's exclusivist creed. It positions IS ideologically against pluralism, democracy and humanism, and implicitly against rival Islamist movements willing to operate within those frameworks. Consistent with periodic identity-reinforcement pieces tied to the Islamic calendar.
notes: Editorial page (page 3) only; remainder of issue not shown. Individuals named are historical/religious figures, not contemporary actors. Geographic focus is umma-wide rather than country-specific.
